items.title: 1348NPRR-01 Telemetry Offset for Provisional Controllable Load Resources 092926
items.explanation: This Nodal Protocol Revision Request (NPRR) introduces a Telemetry Offset framework to bridge the attributability gap between co-located Load and generation. It permits a Qualified Scheduling Entity (QSE) to dynamically raise the telemetered Low Power Consumption (LPC) limit of a Provisional Controllable Load Resource (PCLR) to match the Real-Time Market (RTM) availability of a paired, equivalent mitigating Resource (e.g., Energy Storage System (ESR) or natural gas) on a separate meter. This dynamic telemetry pairing temporarily firms the Load from Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) curtailment while the offsetting capacity is actively offered on an equivalent, offsetting basis. To clear uninstructed Resource deviation flags resulting from this shielded operation, a post-Operating Day Settlement is run, proving the shielded megawatts (MW) were physically backed by the paired Resource. The paired Resource is subjected to the same automatic bid capping methodology as the paired PCLR, ensuring economic equivalency. Finally, it establishes deterministic yielding Protocols requiring the telemetry shield to drop, exposing the Load to curtailment, during system-wide macro-scarcity events.

items.title: 1345NPRR-05 Impact Analysis 092926
items.explanation: This Nodal Protocol Revision Request (NPRR) extends the sunset date established by NPRR1279, Reinstate Enhancements to the Exceptional Fuel Cost Process, from April 1, 2027 to April 1, 2030. The extension preserves the existing review and validation framework for Exceptional Fuel Cost submissions, including supporting documentation and fuel supply contracts submitted under the Exceptional Fuel Cost process, and provides additional time for ERCOT and stakeholders to evaluate long-term enhancements to the treatment of contractual fuel costs while maintaining an existing and operational process that has been actively used since implementation of NPRR1279.
